As the only organization focused exclusively on all of Wright’s remaining buildings, the Conservancy’s work preserves this impactful artistic, cultural, and architectural heritage for today and future generations.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PHOTO 04](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/60e792c6-6ff9-4477-9d48-038c34a46902/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PHOTO_04.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

Photo from The Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation Archives (The Museum of Modern Art | Avery Architectural & Fine Arts Library, Columbia University, New York).

## History: An influential past

With Frank Lloyd Wright being considered one of the greatest American architects, the process began with understanding the legacy, impact, and process behind his work.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PHOTO 26](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/a7650a0f-0708-459e-8c4d-70e514fedd40/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PHOTO_26.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

Photo by Christopher Little courtesy of Western Pennsylvania Conservancy

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PHOTO 03](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/60e792c6-6ff9-4477-9d48-038c34a46902/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PHOTO_03.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C4375%2C5833&w=1000)

With an innovative mind for space, structure, and form, Wright’s buildings redefined the possibilities of architecture.

Photo by Tom Rossiter.

Seeking to strengthen the relationship between how and where people live, Wright believed that “…architecture is life; or at least it is life itself taking form…”.

Throughout his life, Wright developed new categories of architecture and created more than 1,100 designs for government and commercial spaces, hotels, towers, recreational complexes, museums, residential buildings, and more, with nearly half realized.

Today, Wright’s works are still used as museums, studios, residences, and beyond, with their influence continuing to shape the lives of those who visit.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PHOTO 24](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/60e792c6-6ff9-4477-9d48-038c34a46902/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PHOTO_24.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

Photo by Jill Richards.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PHOTO 20](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/60e792c6-6ff9-4477-9d48-038c34a46902/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PHOTO_20.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PHOTO 21](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/60e792c6-6ff9-4477-9d48-038c34a46902/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PHOTO_21.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

However, over time, buildings have been lost to neglect, tragedy, or demolition. In the 1980s, a group of concerned Wright homeowners, architects, scholars, preservationists, and admirers gathered with the goal of protection. As a result of these meetings, in 1989, the Frank Lloyd Wright Building Conservancy was founded.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PHOTO 25](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/60e792c6-6ff9-4477-9d48-038c34a46902/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PHOTO_25.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

Over fifteen percent of Wright’s buildings have been destroyed but with the Conservancy’s work, thousands of members and supporters worldwide have a dedicated network and community of resources, knowledge, and skills to preserve what remains for generations to come.

## Identity: Capturing the community

Built to embrace the span of the community and need for the Conservancy's work, the system balances past, present, and future through form, color, and typography.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 07](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/5596d3dd-cc3a-4d6e-931b-d173c4aa68ff/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_07.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE LOGO 02](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/df73a6d2-2050-41cc-9ba7-8569b7c5c0d6/FLWBC_WEBSITE_LOGO_02.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C4000%2C4000&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PHOTO 22](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/60e792c6-6ff9-4477-9d48-038c34a46902/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PHOTO_22.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

The red square has long been a “signature” throughout all of Wright’s designs, becoming an understood representation of his work.

The identity creates a network with the familiar shape but highlights the impact the loss of even one building has on the larger community.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE LOGO 06 2](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/df3cd077-b3a6-401a-8a66-da8cd1f71a3f/FLWBC_WEBSITE_LOGO_06-2.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C5334&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE SOCIAL 01](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/a882273d-4b7b-4a50-8c87-4a84fbc0c247/FLWBC_WEBSITE_SOCIAL_01.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C4000%2C4000&w=1000)

Through these simple forms, this symbol tells the story of the Conservancy throughout the system.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE LOGO 07](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/df73a6d2-2050-41cc-9ba7-8569b7c5c0d6/FLWBC_WEBSITE_LOGO_07.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE LOGO 08](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/df73a6d2-2050-41cc-9ba7-8569b7c5c0d6/FLWBC_WEBSITE_LOGO_08.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 08](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/51522f5d-10ef-43b6-82d0-9e64ee458501/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_08.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 02](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/5596d3dd-cc3a-4d6e-931b-d173c4aa68ff/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_02.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C4375%2C5833&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE PRINT 01](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/52f43983-a7aa-4468-94e1-dcf7c03b48ca/FLWBC_WEBSITE_PRINT_01.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C4000%2C4000&w=1000)

Used both together and separately, the symbol and wordmark create an adaptive identity toolkit.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE COLOR 02](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/01449a03-4bd1-4738-8d60-691eae28b1e7/FLWBC_WEBSITE_COLOR_02.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

Color is used to express the range of spaces within Wright’s work while adding depth for each value to capture how light and material interact.

In his written communication, Wright had a particular affinity for a typewriter version of Vogue Intertype.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE TYPE 08](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/540efb04-f7f8-4f3c-9ade-f74f27377256/FLWBC_WEBSITE_TYPE_08.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE TYPE 09](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/540efb04-f7f8-4f3c-9ade-f74f27377256/FLWBC_WEBSITE_TYPE_09.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

Wright's use of this typeface inspired [Reply→](https://optimo.ch/typefaces/reply), drawn by François Rappo, which references this pivotal phase in the development of modern American design.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE TYPE 01](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/540efb04-f7f8-4f3c-9ade-f74f27377256/FLWBC_WEBSITE_TYPE_01.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8192%2C5614&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE TYPE 02](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/155cfbfb-e8ea-42dc-8931-c1933e8eb3a7/FLWBC_WEBSITE_TYPE_02.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8192%2C3589&w=1000)

A customized version of Reply from [Optimo Type Foundry→](https://optimo.ch/), is used throughout the identity as the primary voice of the system.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE TYPE 10](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/540efb04-f7f8-4f3c-9ade-f74f27377256/FLWBC_WEBSITE_TYPE_10.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

Characters are rooted in geometric design and American modernism, but bring them forward for contemporary use.

Throughout the identity, the typeface provides an accessible tool to communicate the Conservancy’s work while also capturing the legacy of Wright.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE TYPE 12](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/f22e69f9-3d25-4ccd-bce6-d1b80e97492e/FLWBC_WEBSITE_TYPE_12.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE TYPE 11](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/540efb04-f7f8-4f3c-9ade-f74f27377256/FLWBC_WEBSITE_TYPE_11.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

These angled, geometric forms became a framework for the extended graphic language.

## System: Building a language

In use, the full identity system combines and extends the elements of the toolkit, allowing them to capture the vision of the Conservancy through the individual areas that define it.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 09](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/5596d3dd-cc3a-4d6e-931b-d173c4aa68ff/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_09.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 04](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/5596d3dd-cc3a-4d6e-931b-d173c4aa68ff/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_04.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 05](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/5596d3dd-cc3a-4d6e-931b-d173c4aa68ff/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_05.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

The symbol acts as an anchor throughout the materials.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE ILLUSTRATION 03](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/8d2edc6b-8403-4f23-bce3-00ed4b80fec9/FLWBC_WEBSITE_ILLUSTRATION_03.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

As the story goes, Wright’s fascination with architecture began with a gift of Froebel blocks from his mother. The identity extends this idea through the graphic language of the symbol by creating an illustration system that adapts to each individual structure.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE SOCIAL 03](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/6929cffc-5b01-4eff-bc8f-26cd2e4c67fb/FLWBC_WEBSITE_SOCIAL_03.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

Together, these elements allow the system to capture the wide range of tones and materials throughout the Conservancy’s work.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 10](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/5596d3dd-cc3a-4d6e-931b-d173c4aa68ff/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_10.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)

In addition to the core identity, the symbol is extended to [SaveWright→](https://savewright.org/publications/), the Conservancy’s magazine. This adapted symbol highlights the “missing” square to be saved.

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 01 3](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/39b47f63-e1c3-4cf8-b504-399129607421/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_01-3.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C4000%2C4000&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 06](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/392d1e8a-550c-4ce0-9120-058c5c014497/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_06.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C6250%2C4167&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE APPLICATION 03](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/5596d3dd-cc3a-4d6e-931b-d173c4aa68ff/FLWBC_WEBSITE_APPLICATION_03.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C4375%2C5833&w=1000)

![](data:image/gif;base64,)![FLWBC WEBSITE WEB 02](https://order-site-images-dev.imgix.net/42c4734b-75b2-41b9-9610-3fe61caf5a42/FLWBC_WEBSITE_WEB_02.png?auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=min&fm=png&q=70&rect=0%2C0%2C8000%2C4500&w=1000)
